summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, has become the de facto standard for connecting AI agents to external tools, data, and services through a shared protocol. By 2026, registries like mcpservers.org track over 9,800 servers, and the ecosystem spans aggregator platforms, gateways, and individual servers that let agents read repositories, automate browsers, query databases, and manage workflows. This matters because MCP turns isolated LLMs into capable agents that can act on real systems with standardized auth and tooling.
ecosystem_note: Individual servers (e.g. GitHub MCP, Playwright MCP) each connect an agent to one tool or data source, aggregators (e.g. Composio, Smithery) bundle and manage many servers behind a single interface, and gateways/proxies (e.g. agentgateway, Cloudflare MCP) sit in front of servers to handle auth, routing, and security at scale.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.connects_to: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, and GitHub Actions / CI workflows using GitHub's own identity and permission model
tools.pricing_paid: Free (uses existing GitHub account; GitHub paid plans apply to underlying services)
strengths: Uses GitHub's native identity and permission model
Gold standard for code and CI workflows
tools.best_for: Automating code, repo, and CI/CD workflows directly from an AI agent

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation — navigating pages, filling forms, scraping, and running end-to-end web interactions
strengths: Most-used MCP server in the community (ranked #1 globally in mid-2026 usage rankings)
tools.best_for: Browser automation and web interaction for AI agents

tools.name: Context7 MCP
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date library documentation and code context piped directly into the model
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid Upstash plans for higher usage
strengths: Provides current, version-accurate docs to prevent hallucinated APIs
tools.best_for: Giving coding agents accurate, up-to-date library and framework documentation

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: 250+ tools and apps (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, PostgreSQL, Notion, etc.) with managed OAuth and auth handling
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based paid tiers for higher volume and enterprise features
strengths: 30,000+ GitHub stars and 4,800+ forks (strong community health)
Managed OAuth removes per-server auth burden
Reduces maintenance burden via managed gateway
tools.best_for: Teams that want managed auth and many integrations through one platform

tools.name: Filesystem MCP
tools.connects_to: Local file system — reading, writing, and searching files and directories
strengths: One of the two reference servers almost every stack starts with
No auth required for local access
tools.best_for: Giving agents controlled access to local files and directories

tools.name: Fetch MCP
tools.connects_to: Web content retrieval — fetching and converting URLs/HTML into model-readable content
strengths: Core reference server bundled with most stacks
tools.best_for: Letting agents pull and read live web content

tools.name: Smithery
tools.connects_to: Registry and hosting for thousands of MCP servers with one-click install and configuration across clients
tools.pricing_paid: Paid hosting/enterprise tiers for managed deployments
strengths: Large searchable registry of MCP servers
Popular discovery hub for the ecosystem
tools.best_for: Discovering, installing, and hosting MCP servers quickly

tools.name: Figma MCP
tools.connects_to: Figma design files — extracting layouts, components, and design tokens for design-to-code workflows
tools.pricing_paid: Free with Figma account; Figma paid plans apply to underlying workspace
strengths: Ranked among top servers alongside GitHub and Playwright
tools.best_for: Converting Figma designs into code with AI agents

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Remote MCP hosting and gateway on Cloudflare's edge — deploying, authenticating, and routing MCP servers with OAuth
tools.pricing_paid: Workers/paid plans for higher usage and production deployments
strengths: Edge-hosted remote MCP with built-in OAuth
Scales MCP servers to production reliably
tools.best_for: Deploying and securing remote MCP servers at scale

tools.name: Slack MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Slack workspaces — reading channels, sending messages, and team messaging context
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); Slack paid plans apply to workspace
strengths: Most widely adopted Slack MCP implementation (~1,800 GitHub stars, actively maintained in 2026)
Managed OAuth available via aggregators like Composio
tools.best_for: Bringing Slack team context and messaging into AI agents

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.connects_to: Supabase/Postgres databases — querying, managing schema, and interacting with backend data
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Supabase paid plans for production databases

tools.name: n8n MCP
tools.connects_to: n8n workflow automation — triggering and building automations across 400+ integrated apps
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted; n8n Cloud paid plans for hosted workflows
strengths: Bridges MCP agents with a mature workflow automation platform
Access to hundreds of app integrations via n8n nodes
tools.best_for: Letting agents trigger and orchestrate multi-app automation workflows

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.connects_to: Chrome browser — inspecting the DOM, performance traces, network, and live browser session content
strengths: Deep Chrome inspection and debugging capabilities
Performance and network tracing for agents
tools.best_for: Debugging and inspecting web apps with agents (Chrome only)
